newsitem.title: ANGOLA: COCA-COLA PLANS BOTTLING PLANT FOR ANGOLA.
newsitem.headline: COCA-COLA PLANS BOTTLING PLANT FOR ANGOLA.

text.p: Agreement to build a $20 million Coca-Cola Co bottling plant near Luanda could be reached between the Angolan government and a South African Breweries subsidiary within three months, a Coke representative here said.
"If everything goes according to plan we should have an agreement within three motnhs," said Richard Helmore, Central Africa operations representative for Coke.
"After we have a deal it will take anywhere from 15 to 18 months to build the plant," he said.

South African Breweries bottling unit Indol is currently negotiating with Angola's Ministry of Industry over percentage ownership in the plant and Indol was likely to get a majority ownership, Helmore said.
The plant would have initial capacity of six million cases a year with expansion capability of up to 18 million cases a year.
Its planned site is about 60 km east of Luanda near the village of Bom Jesus on the Kwanza river and would include a franchise area covering the northern part of the country.
"Bom Jesus is a good site for the new plant. The water supply alone makes it a good palce to build," Helmore said.
Bom Jesus free from the water shortages and power outages which plague Luanda.
Prior to independence from Portugal in 1975, Angola had three Coke plants -- in Luanda, the central highlands city of Huambo and the coastal city of Lobito.
But after the country's 20-year civil war only the Huambo plant remains operational.
The Huambo plant has a capacity of 240,000 cases a year and its franchise covers most of central Angola. It is owned by the Angolan company Zuid.
Helmore said that the country's more stable political situation was likely to allow Coke's plan to build the bottling plant to go forward.
